content.title: Tiger Woods arrested for DUI in rollover crash on Jupiter Island, sheriff says
content.text: Golf superstar Tiger Woods was released on bail Friday, hours after his Land Rover clipped a truck, rolled onto its side and he was arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence on Jupiter Island, Florida, officials said. The crash happened just after 2 p.m. along South Beach Road near Hobe Sound Beach, Martin County Sheriff's Office officials said. 6:22Tiger Woods arrested for suspicion of DUI after rollover crash in Florida Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek give updates on a rollover crash involving golfer Tiger Woods on Jupiter Island, Florida, on Friday, March 27, 2026. Woods was arrested for suspicion of DUI. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said Woods was trying to overtake a pressure cleaner truck at a high rate of speed when he clipped the back end of the truck and rolled over his Land Rover. Woods was able to crawl out of the passenger door of the Land Rover and wasn't injured, Budensiek said. The driver of the truck also wasn't injured. But when authorities arrived, Woods appeared to be impaired, Budensiek said. Martin County Sheriff's Office via APMartin County Sheriff's Office via APThis photo provided by the Martin County Sheriff's Office shows the overturned vehicle in a rollover crash which involved Tiger Woods in Jupiter Island, Fla., on Friday, March 27, 2026. "They believe from on scene that he was not impaired on alcohol, they believe that it was some type of medication or drug," Budensiek said. "He was lethargic on scene, but that we believe was because of what he was intoxicated on." Local Woods took a breathalyzer test that didn't detect alcohol but refused to give a urine sample, the sheriff said. "We will never get definitive results as to what he was impaired on at the time of the crash," Budensiek said. Woods was alone in the vehicle, and no drugs or medication were found inside, Budensiek said. Martin County Sheriff's OfficeMartin County Sheriff's OfficeBooking photo of Tiger Woods on March 27, 2026 The sheriff said that Woods was cooperative but "not trying to incriminate himself" and added that he "was careful in what he said and didn't say." The sheriff said Woods was charged for refusing to take the test and DUI with property damage, which are both misdemeanor charges. President Donald Trump, whose former daughter-in-law is dating Tiger Woods, was asked about the golfer when he landed in Miami on Friday afternoon for an investment summit. “I feel so badly. He’s got some difficulty,” Trump said. “Very close friend of mine. He’s an amazing person. Amazing man. But, some difficulty.” Woods, 50, is the most accomplished professional golfer of his generation but has been hampered by injuries in recent years and underwent a seventh back surgery last year. This was the fourth time Woods has been involved in a car crash. He was seriously injured in a car crash in February 2021 that shattered his right leg and ankle, which Woods has said nearly led to a decision to amputate. He was also arrested for DUI in Jupiter back in 2017 and later pleaded guilty to reckless driving in the incident. Woods competed for the first time in more than a year when he played in the TGL final Tuesday night.
